rv.q: The audience is incredibly on board with the company, really ready to assist, to enjoy, to emote.
But it’s a jolly night out, delivered as overwrought idiocy by an amiable cast.
Being wrong has never felt so right!
I was left in stitches and would recommend everyone to catch it on tour before it finishes and is Another Hilarious Masterpiece from Mischief Theatre.
Fabulously inventive and wickedly funny, this iteration of Peter Pan Goes Wrong is expertly performed by a phenomenally talented cast in a production that goes very right indeed.
You’ll be hard pushed to find another show in London that makes you laugh quite as hard as Peter Pan Goes Wrong (except perhaps Mischief’s other show currently playing at the Duchess Theatre).
This show is laugh-out-loud funny throughout, utterly ridiculous, and utterly hysterical. This is a show you can't miss – I can't think of anyone that wouldn't enjoy it!
With a few ups and downs and an akin group of bumps all throughout its delivery, the piece comes out as a slightly enjoyable though, unfortunately, not too memorable experience...

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this gleeful slapstick chaos, praising its relentless physical comedy and theatrical mayhem, though some find the knowing amateur-theater shtick predictable and the humor occasionally one-note.

sg.ra: Closest and most direct view of the stage at Lyric Theatre, with the fullest sound. The standard top pick for any show here.
An elevated, full-stage view with no orchestra-level neck-craning — especially strong for shows with big staging or choreography.
A modest side angle on the stage but still close and clear — a reliable choice when center seats are sold out.

sg.vl: Good sound, check the seat map
sg.ra: Lyric Theatre's own seating notes flag possible obstructed views from the rear orchestra — sound still carries well, but check the seat map before booking here.
At 1,930 seats, Lyric Theatre is one of the larger Broadway houses — far side mezzanine seats sit well off-axis and a long way from the stage.

vs.sum: One of Broadway's largest houses (1,930 seats across four levels), the Lyric's sheer scale means rear orchestra and mezzanine seats sit far from the stage, with sightline obstructions from balcony overhangs. Acoustics are solid and the theater's modern construction makes it well-suited for spectacle productions.

acc.note: 42nd St entrance at street level with elevator to Orchestra and Dress Circle. No elevator to Balcony.
